Hi Jane / Skyline procurement team,

Thanks again for the productive call earlier. As promised, attached is a concise commercial appendix that lays out:
- Unit token pricing (baseline and volume breakpoints)
- Commitment tiers, escrow holdback and phased replenishment mechanics
- Overage handling and pro-rata true-up cadence
- Pilot discounts and graduation path to committed pricing

Key highlights up front:
- Baseline public hosted rate: $0.020 per 1k input tokens / $0.030 per 1k output tokens.
- Offer for Skyline pilot (3 months, up to 50M tokens): 40% pilot discount on baseline.
- Proposed annual commitment: 12M 1k-token units (equivalent to ~12B tokens) with a 6% holdback placed into an escrow account that releases monthly as usage is consumed.
- Overage: billed monthly at committed tier rate + 20% premium, with a pro-rata true-up at quarter end.

We designed the escrow to smooth recognition risk for Skyline and give Redwood a predictable consumption anchor. The mechanics: Redwood invoices the committed amount monthly net of the escrow. If usage exceeds committed buckets in a month, overages draw from escrow first; if escrow is depleted, overage rates apply. At quarter-end we true-up and replenish escrow based on next-quarter commitments or apply crediting.

I've attached a worked example and a draft term sheet. Ben is copied in for any nuances on rate bands and enterprise procurement flow. If helpful, we can convert the same logic to a per-seat or per-concurrent-session construct for your clinical decisioning workloads.

Next steps we suggest:
1) Confirm a pilot start date (we can start within two weeks)
2) Indicate target annual commit band so we can lock-in tiered discounts
3) Share any procurement constraints on escrow/custodian we should plan for

Thanks,

Jane — good questions. I've sketched the numbers below and updated the spreadsheet (see attachment). Key clarifications:

Escrow custody
- We can support a third-party bank escrow or an ACH-locked segregated account. For bank escrow we'll coordinate paperwork and include the custodian name in the SOW.

Worked example (36M 1k-token annual commit; monthly nominal = 3M units):
- 6% escrow = 2.16M units (~$x at tiered rate).
- Usage profile example (month 1 = 50% -> 1.5M; month 2 = 30% -> 0.9M; month 3 = 200% -> 6.0M):
  * Month 1: escrow draws 0; unused portion carries forward into pool; invoice net of escrow.
  * Month 2: same.
  * Month 3: overage draws from escrow first up to escrow balance; remaining overage billed at committed tier + 20% premium.
- Quarter true-up: we true-up at quarter close and either (a) replenish escrow up to 6% of the remaining annual run-rate, or (b) apply invoice credits if consumption is below committed.

Overage caps & throttling
- We can include an automated notification at 85% monthly commit utilization and a soft cap agreement: requests above 140% require pre-approval; automated temporary throttling can be enabled if Skyline requests it.

Pilot discount applicability
- Pilot discount (40%) applies to hosted deployments. For Dedicated deployments we offer a tailored pilot pricing (typically 25–35% depending on duration and reserved GPU hours) because Dedicated includes infra reservation costs. We can map the pilot credit to a one-time invoice credit if you move from Hosted -> Dedicated within 90 days.

Additional optional items
- QoS SLA credits tied to 95th percentile tail latency for dedicated pools.
- Optional monthly usage smoothing (automatic pre-billing to build a buffer pool).

I added Marissa to help with contract language and to expedite term-sheet redlines. Attached: proposed_term_sheet_skyline.xlsx (tab "Escrow worked example").
